Definition: Integration of company registration, business licensing, tax compliance, regulatory compliance data
Comments: BRELA (Business Registrations and Licensing Agency) connected to GovESB. Business registration data partially integrated with government data exchange platform. e-Government Strategy references business service integration.
revision_notes: Original sources cited (govesb.gov.go.tz, e-strategy PDF) were fetched: the GovESB URL is a bare loading page with no substantive content, and the e-strategy PDF could not be retrieved (timeout), so neither source actually supports the claim as cited. Fresh checks confirm BRELA runs two online platforms - the established Online Registration System (ORS) and a newly launched (April 2026) Online Services (BOS) system - covering registration, licensing, trademarks and patents. A "Jamii Startup" module is referenced as part of the wider Jamii Stack/GovESB ecosystem, but no source demonstrates live, automated cross-agency data flow (e.g. to TRA or NBS) via the data exchange. Score of 3 (Under development) is confirmed on the newer evidence; not upgraded given lack of proof of operational integration.
revised_comments: BRELA operates two online platforms for business registration and licensing: the established Online Registration System (ORS) and the newly launched (April 2026) Online Services (BOS) system, covering business name registration, company incorporation, industrial licensing, trademarks and patents. Business registration data is not yet confirmed to flow automatically through the GovESB/Jamii X-Change interoperability layer to other government agencies such as tax or statistics bodies; a "Jamii Startup" module is referenced within the wider Tanzania technology stack, but detailed evidence of live cross-agency integration is not available. Integration of business registration and licensing data with the national data exchange remains under development.

Definition: Extent to which the national digital identity system is integrated with the data exchange for identity verification and authentication
Comments: NIDA (National Identification Authority) national ID system exists. Jamii X-Change uses once-only principle for identity verification across agencies. Integration under development; not yet fully operational across all government systems.
revision_notes: The dpi.africa.com case study was fetched and confirms Jamii Namba (digital ID) and describes Jamii X-Change as the data exchange platform; govesb.gov.go.tz itself remains a bare loading page with no substantive detail. Fresh searches show Jamii X-Change (the data exchange) went live in January 2025 and is built specifically around identity verification and the once-only principle, with documented sector use cases (education/RITA civil registration, financial services) that authenticate against Jamii Namba records, and 300-400 public/private systems reportedly interacting through it. This is materially more advanced than "under development" as of 2023, so the score is revised upward to 4 (Partially integrated); full nationwide operability is not yet evidenced, so not raised further.
revised_comments: Tanzania's digital identity system, Jamii Namba, is integrated with the national data exchange platform, Jamii X-Change (also known as Jamii Data Shirikishi), which went live in January 2025. Jamii X-Change is built around identity verification and the once-only principle, enabling cross-agency and cross-sector authentication; documented use cases include validating identity records against national identification systems for education (examination councils, RITA civil registration) and other sectors. Over 300-400 public and private sector systems reportedly interact through the exchange. Full nationwide interoperability across all government services is still being scaled, so integration is regarded as partial rather than complete.

Definition: Integration of health records, patient registration, immunization data, and health insurance into data exchange
Comments: Tanzania Health Information Exchange (Tz-HIE) operational since approximately 2019 with 15 health systems integrated. DHIS2 in use. Health sector leads government data exchange integration efforts. Partially integrated with broader GovESB.
revision_notes: dpi.africa.com case study fetched and confirms the health sector's role in Tanzania's digital economy strategy; govesb.gov.go.tz remains a bare loading page and adds nothing. A further search on Jamii Wallet (2025) confirms health data is one of the core categories consolidated for citizens via the Jamii X-Change ecosystem, consistent with continued partial integration. Score of 4 (Partially integrated) is confirmed unchanged; no evidence found of full/comprehensive integration.
revised_comments: Tanzania operates a health information exchange (Tz-HIE), operational since around 2019 using DHIS2, linking approximately 15 discrete health information systems. Health data is one of the core categories accessible through the emerging Jamii Wallet application, part of the Jamii X-Change interoperability platform launched in January 2025, giving citizens a consolidated profile spanning health, demographic and education records. Integration with the broader Government Enterprise Service Bus is substantial but not yet comprehensive across the whole health sector.

Definition: Integration with national payment systems for government-to-person (G2P), government-to-business (G2B) transactions via data exchange
Comments: Tanzania has government payment gateways (GePG) and mobile money integration. GovESB connects financial systems. Partial integration with national payment infrastructure documented but full G2P/G2B interoperability through a single exchange not confirmed.
revision_notes: govesb.gov.go.tz is a bare loading page and the e-strategy PDF could not be retrieved, so neither original source substantiates the score. The DPI Exemplar case study (fetched) documents that GePG (revenue collection) and TIPS (instant payments linking banks and mobile money) are both integrated under the Jamii Malipo/Jamii X-Change ecosystem, with government revenue collected digitally rising from roughly TZS 951 billion (2018) to TZS 4.3 trillion (2022) and about 80% of the population holding a reachable financial account. This is stronger evidence of functioning integration than "under development", so the score is revised upward to 4 (Partially integrated).
revised_comments: Tanzania's national payment gateway (GePG) and instant payment system (TIPS) are integrated with government revenue collection and are increasingly linked through the Jamii Malipo component of the Jamii Stack, alongside the Jamii X-Change interoperability layer. Government revenue collected through digital payment channels rose from roughly TZS 951 billion to TZS 4.3 trillion between 2018 and 2022, and around 80% of the population hold a financial account reachable through these rails. Digital payments integration into the data exchange is functioning for a substantial share of government-to-person and government-to-business transactions, though it is not yet comprehensive across all payment types and agencies.

Definition: Integration of statistics, census data, administrative data for planning, M&E, and evidence-based policymaking
Comments: NBS (National Bureau of Statistics) Tanzania and planning agencies connected via GovESB ecosystem. E-Government Strategy references integration of statistics for national planning. Partial integration documented.
revision_notes: govesb.gov.go.tz is a bare loading page and the e-strategy PDF could not be retrieved, so the original sources do not substantiate the claim as cited. Fresh research shows NBS and OCGS have a 2024 manual for integrating administrative data (e.g. from TRA) into official statistics, and produced a first joint Statistical Business Register update using administrative sources in 2023/24. This confirms active integration work but does not establish that data flows specifically through GovESB/Jamii X-Change rather than bespoke bilateral agreements. Score of 3 (Under development) is confirmed unchanged given the absence of clear evidence of exchange-platform-based integration.
revised_comments: The National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) and the Office of the Chief Government Statistician are pursuing closer integration of administrative data - including from the Tanzania Revenue Authority and business registration sources - into official statistics, formalised through a 2024 manual for integrating administrative data and a first joint Statistical Business Register update using administrative sources in 2023/24. Clear evidence that this data flows specifically through the government's central data exchange (GovESB/Jamii X-Change), rather than through bespoke bilateral data-sharing arrangements, is not yet available, so integration into the whole-of-government exchange remains under development.

Definition: Integration of tax administration and revenue collection systems data into the exchange platform
Comments: TRA (Tanzania Revenue Authority) connected to GovESB ecosystem. Data sharing with tax systems referenced in e-Gov Strategy. Full integration not confirmed with clear evidence.
revision_notes: govesb.gov.go.tz is a bare loading page and the e-strategy PDF could not be retrieved. The Jamii X-Change "about" page (jxrportaldemo.nida.go.tz, an official NIDA-hosted portal) explicitly states the platform "enables secure sharing of financial data between tax authorities, financial institutions, and businesses... supporting real-time updates and automated reporting", building on the GovESB data-sharing framework already mandated under the e-Government Act 2019. This is direct, authoritative evidence that TRA integration is now functioning rather than merely planned, so the score is revised upward to 4 (Partially integrated).
revised_comments: The Tanzania Revenue Authority is connected to the national interoperability platform, Jamii X-Change, which is explicitly designed to enable secure sharing of financial data between tax authorities, financial institutions and businesses, supporting real-time updates and automated reporting to improve compliance monitoring. This builds on the earlier Government Enterprise Service Bus (GovESB), established under the e-Government Act 2019, through which TRA systems already exchanged data with other public institutions. Tax and revenue data integration into the exchange is functioning for core use cases, though not yet comprehensive across all tax types and cross-border scenarios.

Definition: Whether primary laws, acts, or legal instruments exist that establish authority for cross-government data sharing and govern the data exchange system
Comments: e-Government Act 2019 Section 28(g) mandates public institutions to maintain interoperable systems. e-Government General Regulations 2020 Section 59(1) covers GovESB mandate. E-Government Interoperability Framework adopted 2017, made mandatory under 2019 Act. Personal Data Protection Act also enacted.
revision_notes: govesb.gov.go.tz is a bare loading page; the dpi.africa.com case study (fetched) confirms the Personal Data Protection Act, 2022 as part of the regulatory environment but does not itself detail the e-Government Act. Fresh review of the primary legal text (TanzLII) confirms Sections 47-49 of the e-Government Act, 2019 require electronic data sharing and mandate the e-Government Authority to establish and manage a data-sharing/exchange platform, operationalised via the 2020 General Regulations (Section 59) and subsequent GovESB technical criteria (2022). Score of 3 (Yes) is confirmed unchanged; legislation clearly exists and is in force.
revised_comments: Tanzania's e-Government Act, 2019 (Sections 47-49) establishes the legal mandate for public institutions to share data electronically and requires the e-Government Authority to establish and manage a data-sharing and exchange platform, the Government Enterprise Service Bus (GovESB). The e-Government General Regulations, 2020 (Section 59) and subsequent technical criteria documents operationalise this mandate, and the Personal Data Protection Act, 2022 provides the accompanying data protection framework. Primary legislation establishing authority for the data exchange is firmly in place.

Definition: Provisions ensuring national control over government data and protecting against unauthorized foreign access
Comments: Personal Data Protection Act enacted (referenced in EAC comparative study). e-Government Act 2019 Section 28(g) mandates government data interoperability standards. Cross-border transfer provisions included but enforcement capacity limited. Data sovereignty provisions exist but enforcement is nascent.
revision_notes: dpi.africa.com case study (fetched) confirms enactment of the Personal Data Protection Act, 2022 but predates enforcement activity; govesb.gov.go.tz is a bare loading page. The primary Act text confirms Part V requires a Commission permit before personal data leaves the country, with enforcement notices and fines up to TZS 100 million (Sections 45-47). Crucially, fresh evidence shows the Personal Data Protection Commission (launched April 2024) has since moved from dormant to active: it set and enforced a compulsory registration deadline (April 2025) with threatened legal sanctions, and in 2025 issued its first rulings with monetary fines/damages against violators. This demonstrates real enforcement, not merely unenforced controls, so the score is revised upward to 4 (Strong, enforced controls).
revised_comments: Tanzania's Personal Data Protection Act, 2022 establishes restrictions on the cross-border transfer of personal data (Part V), requiring a permit from the Personal Data Protection Commission (PDPC) before data may leave the country, alongside enforcement notices and administrative fines of up to TZS 100 million for non-compliance. The PDPC, launched in April 2024, has since actively enforced the Act: it required mandatory registration of all data controllers and processors by April 2025, with threatened legal action for non-compliance, and in 2025 issued its first monetary rulings and fines against violators. Controls over national data and cross-border flows are both substantive in law and now backed by demonstrated regulatory enforcement.
